items.text: Pressing Enter at the very start of a page's properties (click the page properties, move the caret to the start, press Enter) no longer stops the page saving with "Couldn't save … Tine keeps trying" and leaves every later edit on that page unsaved. As in Logseq, Enter there adds a line inside the properties, which is dropped when you leave them; the properties stay the page header. Moving a block above the page properties (Alt+Shift+Up on the first block, or dropping a block above them) is now refused for the same reason. A page left in that state by an earlier build saves again once you delete the empty block above its properties (GH #210 F1).

items.text: **Typing in the Search tab (and the `((` block picker) can no longer end on "Search superseded by a newer request" with no results**: when the search for an earlier keystroke reached the search engine after the search for the latest one, it cancelled the latest. Each search now carries the order it was issued in, and the engine ignores one that was overtaken (REG-OG-SEARCH-LANE-ORDER).

regressionEvidence.reason: Catalog coverage: REG-OG-SEARCH-LANE-ORDER (fail-before proven: both lane-order Rust tests and the backend laneSeq test fail before the fix; a 40-retype native loop stuck once on the unfixed binary). The native scenario e2e-search-tab-keyboard.mjs is the control; the race is timing-dependent, so a green native run is not proof of absence. Linux only; other platforms unverified.

docs.reason: Restores search results under fast typing; the Guide never described the superseded-search message.

items.text: Windows portable: the portable ZIP now keeps Tine's settings, sessions, backups, plugins, diagnostics and WebView2 data in a `tine-data` folder next to `Tine.exe` instead of in `%APPDATA%` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, so Tine runs from a USB drive without leaving app data on the computer (GH #719). It is the `tine-data` folder in the ZIP that makes Tine portable; the installer and the Microsoft Store app are unchanged. A portable Tine offers new versions as a download instead of running the installer, which would have added an installed copy. Earlier portable runs left their settings in AppData; Tine does not move or delete them, and `tine-data\README.txt` says how to copy them over. If the `tine-data` folder cannot be written, Tine does not start and says which folder to move; it never falls back to AppData. A `tine-data` folder inside an installed Tine's folder, or a link named `tine-data`, does not make it portable.

regressionEvidence.reason: Catalog coverage: REG-GH719-PORTABLE-HOST-WRITES (fail-before proven at the unit layer on release/0.8 4e389bcfe, plus review r1's single-probe install test). The Windows journey e2e-windows-portable.mjs (real exe, real AppData) is pending a hosted run per the catalog row; nothing in this prep ran on Windows.

Troubleshooting already names the portable log folder.
